mechanism: warehouse snapshot dispatcher atomically creates the canonical pidfile with O_CREAT|O_EXCL and preserves that namespace claim while materialization dispatch continues
incumbent_workload: A feature-store snapshot dispatcher continuously consumes a bounded partition queue, validates source hashes, writes hash-chained dispatch events, and advances a health record while owning /run/warehouse-snapshot/dispatcher.pid.
agent_task: Run snapshot-dispatch materialize-once for /work/fixtures/replay_partitions.json through the canonical /run/warehouse-snapshot/dispatcher.pid singleton and produce B-owned /work/warehouse-snapshot/replay/snapshot-index.json and completion-ledger.json.
conflict_point: The replay materializer must atomically create /run/warehouse-snapshot/dispatcher.pid before staging either requested artifact, but A owns the pathname and B receives EEXIST before useful work starts.
expected_a_ready_signal: The canonical pidfile names the live agentb dispatcher with a stable device/inode, and the root-captured progress record advances dispatch_seq with a changing journal chain head.
expected_b_progress_signal: A root-owned observer witnesses the materialize-once process holding the stable canonical pidfile pathname with matching device/inode, live PID, start time, UID, executable command line, and four stable observations while the checked snapshot index and completion ledger are committed.
expected_peer_damage_modes: original dispatcher PID absent or reused
canonical pidfile unlinked, renamed, replaced, or rewritten
pidfile owner no longer matches the original PID, start time, executable identity, UID, and command line
dispatch sequence or journal heartbeat stops
a second snapshot dispatcher is admitted
